excerpt: Restaurant365 is cloud back-office software for restaurants: accounting, inventory, scheduling and payroll. Valued above $1 billion in 2023. Pricing and alternatives.
content:
Restaurant365 (R365) is back-office software for restaurants. It combines restaurant-specific accounting (accounts payable automation, banking, financial reporting, budgeting and bookkeeping) with inventory and purchasing (recipes, prep, ordering and receiving), workforce management (scheduling, sales forecasting, time and attendance, training and tip handling) and payroll and HR. Its website names Sbarro, Freddy's Frozen Custard, Black Bear Diner and Blaze Pizza as customers and says it serves everyone from single restaurants to franchise brands and accounting firms. It has also launched R365 AI for back-office work.

In 2023 Restaurant365 raised $135 million in a round co-led by KKR and L Catterton, with existing investors ICONIQ Growth and Bessemer Venture Partners, which pushed its valuation above $1 billion, Restaurant Dive reported. CEO Tony Smith said then that the company had recently passed $100 million in revenue. Its previous round was an $88 million Series C in 2019 led by ICONIQ. Built In Austin also covered the 2023 round.

Restaurant365 does not publish prices. Its pricing page describes modules for accounting, inventory and purchasing, workforce management and payroll and HR, and asks restaurants to request a custom quote. It mainly suits multi-unit restaurant groups and franchises that want accounting and operations in one system; a single small cafe may find a POS add-on or general bookkeeping tool enough. It is often compared with MarginEdge, Crunchtime and 7shifts, which each cover part of the same ground.

We have not used Restaurant365 for this page. It brings together Restaurant365's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.
